title: Resolve the effective device before capability caching or CUDA stream dispatch
applies_when: A capability, current_stream or kernel-dispatch helper defaults to the current accelerator, especially when tensors may be on a noncurrent device or the current device can change.
lesson: A no-argument cache stores the first current-device answer, not a device-independent fact. Resolve the actual device index before the per-device cache and route tensor-dependent dispatch from the tensor's device. Test both switch orders with differing capabilities, explicit-device calls, cache reuse and the non-CUDA fallback. CUDA current-stream state is also per device: current_stream() queries the process's current device, not the input tensor's device. Use distinct nondefault streams on two devices to expose that mismatch; default stream handles alone can hide it. Check same-device and explicit-stream controls and record the backend's device_id with the stream. A mocked query or intercepted launch can establish selection semantics; keep native operator qualification separate.
avoid_when: Even homogeneous GPUs can have different current streams. A stable CUDA ordinal is a process-local identity, not a portable hardware profile or live resource allocation. Simulated capability queries do not prove mixed-hardware execution, PDL compatibility or performance. Real Torch stream selection with the final backend call intercepted is not TileLang kernel numerical or launch-context qualification. A device-scoped query alone does not establish that the native context, allocations and kernel handles agree. Preserve explicit caller streams; CPU, no-tensor and mixed-device input paths need their own contracts.

evidence.note: The original supports_pdl has a no-argument lru_cache and queries the current CUDA device, exposing the stale-answer mechanism after a device switch.

Proposed, unmerged fix includes seven CPU regressions using the real standalone utility module with mocked backend/device queries. Tests cover both switch orders, explicit device indices, property-cache reuse and non-CUDA fallback. They are not native mixed-GPU or operator performance evidence.
The exact Torch API documents device=None as the current CUDA device and passes the resolved device index to _cuda_getCurrentStream; it does not infer a tensor device.

Contributor-tested exact PR wrapper methods on two RTX5090s with Torch2.11 native tensors/streams: both noncurrent-device cases select the other device's stream; same-device, explicit-stream and device-scoped controls agree. Final backend calls were intercepted. No compiled TileLang kernel, numerical qualification, full current-main build or author acceptance is claimed.
